description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotional categories in a dataset used for evaluating speaker anonymization on emotional speech, with six distinct emotion labels represented as colored segments. The largest segment, labeled “Frustration,” occupies 25.1% of the chart and is colored light blue. The second largest, “Neutral,” accounts for 23.1% and is shown in dark blue. “Excitement” follows at 14.1%, depicted in red; “Sadness” at 14.9%, in orange; “Anger” at 14.9%, in yellow; and “Happiness” is the smallest segment at 8.1%, colored light purple. Each slice is clearly labeled with its emotion name and percentage value, and the chart uses a standard circular layout with no exploded segments or 3D effects. The visual proportions align with the numerical values, suggesting a relatively balanced distribution across most emotions, except for “Happiness,” which is notably underrepresented. No legend is present, as labels are directly placed on or adjacent to each slice.
